title: WHY EVERYONE DID WHAT WAS RIGHT IN THEIR OWN EYES
paragraphs: WHY EVERYONE DID WHAT WAS RIGHT IN THEIR OWN EYES
The Ancient Warning That Sounds Exactly Like Today
By Gospel Warrior
There is a sentence buried in the Book of Judges that feels less like ancient history and more like tomorrow's headline.
A civilization collapsing.
Families breaking apart.
Violence increasing.
Truth becoming negotiable.
Morality becoming personalized.
Everyone becoming their own authority.
And then Scripture delivers its haunting diagnosis:
"In those days there was no king in Israel. Everyone did what was right in his own eyes." (Judges 21:25)
The Hebrew is even more powerful.

אִישׁ הַיָּשָׁר בְּעֵינָיו יַעֲשֶׂה
('ish hayashar be'enav ya'aseh)
Literally:
"A man would do what was straight in his own eyes."
Notice what the text does not say.
It does not say people were trying to do evil.
It says they were doing what seemed right.
That is what makes this passage so terrifying.
Human beings rarely destroy themselves while consciously pursuing evil.
They destroy themselves while pursuing a version of good disconnected from God.
And that ancient disease still lives inside every human heart.
Not just society.
Not just politicians.
Not just culture.
Us.
The reason this story still hurts is because every one of us has lived it.
Every one of us has trusted our own wisdom over God's.
Every one of us has rewritten truth to accommodate desire.
Every one of us has looked at something God called dangerous and convinced ourselves it was harmless.
Every one of us has stared into a mirror and declared ourselves qualified to be our own king.
That is the story of Judges.
And that is the story of humanity.
The Book of Judges is one of the darkest books in Scripture.
It is not dark because God failed.
It is dark because people repeatedly rejected Him.
The book follows a devastating cycle.
Israel sins.
God allows consequences.
The people cry out.
God sends a deliverer.
The people experience restoration.
Then they repeat the entire process again.
And again.
And again.
Every generation thinks it can handle autonomy better than the generation before it.
Every generation discovers it cannot.
What makes Judges so emotionally exhausting is that the decline is gradual.
Nobody wakes up and decides to collapse a nation.
Compromise happens one decision at a time.
A little less obedience.
A little less reverence.
A little less truth.
A little more self.
Until eventually everyone becomes their own authority.
And when everyone becomes their own authority, chaos becomes inevitable.
The human heart was never designed to sit on God's throne.
The prophet Jeremiah understood this reality with painful clarity.
The original Hebrew reads:

עָקֹב הַלֵּב מִכֹּל
('aqov halev mikol)
"The heart is deceitful above all things." (Jeremiah 17:9)
The word 'aqov carries the idea of something twisted, crooked, or deceptive.
The problem is not merely that our hearts can be wrong.
The problem is that our hearts can convince us they are right while being wrong.
That is exactly what happened in Judges.
And it is exactly what happens now.
Our culture often celebrates authenticity as the highest virtue.
"Follow your heart."
"Live your truth."
"Be true to yourself."
Those phrases sound liberating.
Until we realize they are asking broken people to trust broken instincts.
Scripture never teaches us to follow our hearts.
Scripture teaches us to surrender our hearts.
Those are two radically different things.
The Bible presents an uncomfortable truth modern humanity struggles to accept.
God is not simply a helpful advisor.
He is King.
The Hebrew word often used is מֶלֶךְ (melech).
King.
Ruler.
Sovereign.
Authority.
The tragedy of Judges is not merely that Israel lacked a political king.
The deeper issue was that they stopped recognizing God's kingship.
When God's authority is rejected, something else always fills the vacuum.
Self.
Desire.
Power.
Pleasure.
Money.
Popularity.
Politics.
Identity.
Something always takes the throne.
Human beings were created to worship.
If we refuse to worship God, we simply worship something else.
The New Testament reveals this problem even more clearly.
Jesus arrives in a world filled with people who believed they were spiritually fine.
Religious leaders trusted themselves.
Political leaders trusted themselves.
The wealthy trusted themselves.
The powerful trusted themselves.
The educated trusted themselves.
Then Jesus began dismantling every illusion.
One of the most significant Greek words in the New Testament is:

μετάνοια
(metanoia)
Usually translated as "repentance."
But its meaning is deeper than many realize.
It literally describes a change of mind that produces a change of direction.
Repentance is not merely feeling bad.
Repentance is surrendering self-rule.
It is stepping off the throne.
It is admitting:
"I am not the king."
That is why the Gospel is offensive.
The Gospel does not simply offer help.
It challenges authority.
Not Rome's authority.
Not Caesar's authority.
Yours.
Mine.
The Gospel announces that Jesus Christ is Lord.
The Greek declaration used by early Christians was:

Ἰησοῦς Κύριος
(Iēsous Kyrios)
"Jesus is Lord."
To modern ears that sounds like religious language.
To first-century ears it was revolutionary.
Because if Jesus is Lord, then I am not.
If Jesus is King, then my feelings are not.
If Jesus is Truth, then my opinions do not determine reality.
If Jesus reigns, then my life belongs to Him.
That is the dividing line of every generation.
Not whether people acknowledge God exists.
But whether they will surrender to His authority.
The frightening reality is that Judges is not ultimately a story about Israel.
It is a story about humanity.
Left to ourselves, we drift.
Left to ourselves, we compromise.
Left to ourselves, we redefine truth.
Left to ourselves, we crown ourselves king.
Yet woven through the darkness of Judges is an extraordinary hope.
God never stopped pursuing His people.
Again and again they failed.
Again and again He rescued.
Again and again He showed mercy.
Again and again He made a way back.
That relentless mercy points forward to Jesus Christ.
The true King Israel needed.
The true King humanity needs.
The true King your heart needs.
Because the solution to a world where everyone does what is right in their own eyes is not better politics.
It is not stronger willpower.
It is not greater education.
It is not self-improvement.
It is a new King.
The Gospel begins where self-rule ends.
Maybe that is why this ancient verse still feels so personal.
Most people reading this are not wrestling with ancient Israel.
They are wrestling with themselves.
The private compromise.
The hidden addiction.
The bitterness nobody sees.
The pride disguised as independence.
The fear disguised as control.
The rebellion disguised as freedom.
And maybe the Holy Spirit is asking a question that cuts deeper than any political debate or cultural argument ever could:
Who sits on the throne of your life?
Be honest.
Not who attends church.
Not who owns a Bible.
Not who claims Christianity.
Who actually rules your decisions?
Who determines your values?
Who defines truth?
Who occupies the throne?
Because every human heart eventually chooses one of two kings.
Self.
Or Christ.
And only one of them died to save you.
The most dangerous throne in the world is the one hidden inside the human heart.
